test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Fitter) Official Paper (Held On: 02 May, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following statements correctly describes the placement and purpose of orientation marks on a drawing sheet?

1. Orientation marks are placed at two opposite corners of the drawing sheet to indicate the correct orientation on the drawing board.

2. Orientation marks consist of arrow heads placed across the frame, with one at the shorter side and one at the longer side, coinciding with the centering marks.

3. One of the orientation marks always points towards the draughtsman, indicating the direction in which the drawing sheet should be placed.

4. Orientation marks are used to mark the midpoint of each side of the drawing sheet for accurate centering.
solution:
__**Explanation:**__

**Orientation Marks on a Drawing Sheet**

 
• Orientation marks are specific indicators placed on a drawing sheet to guide the draughtsman in ensuring the sheet is properly aligned on the drawing board. These marks help avoid errors in the orientation of the drawing during the drafting process and ensure accuracy in the representation of design elements.

**Correct Option Analysis:**

The correct option is:

**Option 4:** Orientation marks are used to mark the midpoint of each side of the drawing sheet for accurate centering.

This option correctly describes the purpose of orientation marks. These marks are positioned at the midpoint of each side of the drawing sheet to assist the draughtsman in aligning the sheet accurately on the drawing board. Accurate centering is essential for achieving precision in engineering drawings, especially when working with large-scale designs or templates.

**Purpose of Orientation Marks:**

 
• Assist in aligning the drawing sheet accurately on the drawing board.
 
• Ensure the design elements are properly oriented and symmetrical.
 
• Facilitate easy identification of the correct orientation during the drafting process.

**Placement of Orientation Marks:**

 
• Orientation marks are placed at the midpoint of each side of the drawing sheet.
 
• These marks are often small crosses or dots, indicating the center points of the edges of the sheet.
 
• They act as reference points for aligning the sheet with the T-square or other drafting tools.

**Advantages:**

 
• Improves the accuracy of the drawings by ensuring proper alignment.
 
• Prevents errors due to incorrect orientation of the drawing sheet.
 
• Makes it easier to create symmetrical designs and patterns.
